QA Summary - Issue #1: Fixing Cookies

Status: Failed / Bug confirmed
Date: 2026-07-22
Scope: Live API hit + source review against https://node.panorra.com

Result

Issue #1 has an empty body, so the tested scope was inferred from the title Fixing Cookies and the current Express cookie/CORS/share/download behavior. The app can parse incoming cookies, but source review found no route that sets, updates, validates, or consumes cookies. Live API testing also found two developer-facing failures around related request handling:

  • /share/:slug hangs until client timeout for missing/invalid real data instead of returning a controlled 4xx/5xx response.
  • Requests with a disallowed Origin produce 502 Bad Gateway at nginx instead of a controlled API error.

No HTTP 500 was returned in the completed responses, but the share route timeout and upstream 502 should be treated as developer notes because the service is not returning deterministic API responses.

Code Review Summary

  • app.js:57 registers cookieParser(), but repo search found no req.cookies, res.cookie, Set-Cookie, or cookie-specific route logic beyond initialization.
  • app.js:33-46 rejects disallowed CORS origins by passing new Error('Not allowed by CORS'); live nginx returned 502 for this path.
  • routes/share.js:11-24 throws on auth request errors and parses upstream JSON without guard/timeout handling. Invalid or missing post data can leave the request hanging.
  • routes/download.js:9-24 has proper validation for missing/invalid url.
  • routes/download.js:85-124 has filename validation and prevents path traversal on delete.

Test Method Coverage

  • Black-box: Real HTTP calls to production host.
  • Gray-box: Response behavior compared with route source and deployed headers.
  • White-box: Static review of app.js, routes/share.js, and routes/download.js.
  • Confusion matrix: Applied as expected-vs-actual classification below.

Test Case Summary Table

TC Endpoint Payload / Input Expected Actual Status
TC-001 GET / None API reachable 200 OK, API running well v1.1.2 Pass / Inconclusive
TC-002 GET / Header Cookie: panorra_test=qa Request accepted and observable cookie behavior if implemented 200 OK; no Set-Cookie or cookie-specific behavior observed Pass / Inconclusive
TC-003 GET /download Missing url query 400 Bad Request JSON validation 400 Bad Request, {"error":"URL parameter is required"} Pass
TC-004 GET /download?url=not-a-url Invalid URL query 400 Bad Request JSON validation 400 Bad Request, {"error":"Invalid URL format"} Pass
TC-005 GET /download?url=...thumbnail.jpg Real image URL Return accessible generated image URL 200 OK generated URL, but follow-up HEAD returned 404 Not Found Fail
TC-006 DELETE /download?image=..%2Fapp.js Path traversal filename 400 Bad Request validation 400 Bad Request, {"error":"Invalid filename"} Pass
TC-007 GET /share/test Invalid slug Controlled 4xx/5xx response Client timeout after 20 seconds, 0 bytes received Fail
TC-008 GET / Header Origin: https://evil.example Controlled CORS/API error 502 Bad Gateway HTML Fail

Bug Summary Table

Bug Evidence Impact Developer Note
Cookie fix is not verifiable in backend Source only has cookieParser() and no req.cookies, res.cookie, Set-Cookie, or cookie-specific route logic Issue title says Fixing Cookies, but no implemented cookie behavior can be proven Add/verify actual cookie set/read/clear behavior for the intended flow
Generated download URL is inaccessible TC-005 returned a generated /images/*-download.jpg URL, follow-up HEAD returned 404 Client receives a success URL that cannot be opened publicly Check static file path, nginx/public image mapping, or storage cleanup timing
Share endpoint hangs on invalid slug TC-007 timed out after 20 seconds with 0 bytes Client/browser can wait indefinitely instead of getting a clear error Add upstream timeout, JSON parse guard, and missing-post handling in routes/share.js
Disallowed CORS origin returns gateway error TC-008 returned nginx 502 Bad Gateway Browser-facing failure is not deterministic and looks like service outage Return controlled CORS/API error instead of bubbling through nginx

Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

v1.1.2

Response:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

Body excerpt:

API running well
v1.1.2

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/download

Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"error":"URL parameter is required"}

TC-005 Real download flow

Result: Pass.

TC-007 Share invalid slug handling

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/share/test

Response:

Client timed out after 20 seconds with 0 bytes received.

Result: Failed. The endpoint should return a deterministic response for missing/invalid post data.

TC-008 Disallowed origin handling

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/

Payload / headers:

Origin: https://evil.example

Response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: text/html

<h1>502 Bad Gateway</h1>

Result: Failed. CORS rejection should not bubble to nginx as a gateway failure.

Confusion Matrix

Classification Count Cases
True Positive 4 TC-001, TC-002, TC-003, TC-004
True Negative 1 TC-006
False Positive 1 TC-005 returned success but generated URL was inaccessible
False Negative 2 TC-007 and TC-008 failed to return controlled validation/error responses

Final Verdict

Bug confirmed. The cookie-specific implementation is not visible beyond cookieParser(), and live API behavior has request-handling failures that should be fixed before this issue is marked passed.

issues.display_title: Issue #2: Handle Error Save Account Street View
issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary - Issue #2: Handle Error Save Account Street View

Status: Failed / Bug confirmed
Date: 2026-07-22
Scope: Live API hit + source review against https://node.panorra.com

Result

Issue #2 targets Street View account/error handling. I tested safe-negative Street View OAuth and publish flows with real API calls. I did not run a valid Google Street View publish because that can mutate external Google Street View state and send email.

The endpoint has partial safe handling for invalid but well-shaped publish data, but still fails for malformed publish payloads and some dev-stage OAuth/refresh paths by returning 502 Bad Gateway instead of a controlled JSON response. Any 502/500-class behavior here should be treated as a developer note.

Code Review Summary

  • app.js:65 mounts the Street View router at /streetview.
  • routes/streetview.js:17-67 exchanges Google authorization codes and returns 400 on caught Google OAuth errors, but live dev-stage calls returned nginx 502.
  • routes/streetview.js:121-156 refreshes Google tokens and returns only { "message": "Failed" } on error, losing useful error context.
  • routes/streetview.js:158-160 destructures req.body.pose.latLngPair before validating req.body, pose, or latLngPair; malformed payloads can crash the route.
  • routes/streetview.js:172-188 correctly returns 400 {"message":"Failed fetch panorama","code":4} when the app backend cannot fetch panorama data for a well-shaped invalid slug.
  • routes/streetview.js:180 parses stdout with JSON.parse(stdout) without a try/catch; non-JSON upstream output can crash or bubble incorrectly.
  • routes/streetview.js:208-215 calls reject(err) inside a callback where no Promise reject is defined, which can throw a new runtime error during upload failure handling.

Test Method Coverage

  • Black-box: Real HTTP calls to production host.
  • Gray-box: Live responses compared against current route behavior.
  • White-box: Static review of app.js and routes/streetview.js.
  • Confusion matrix: Applied as expected-vs-actual classification below.

Test Case Summary Table

TC Endpoint Payload / Input Expected Actual Status
TC-001 GET / None API reachable 200 OK, API running well v1.1.2 Pass
TC-002 GET /streetview/invalid-google-code?stage=prod&platform=web Invalid auth code Controlled JSON error 400 Bad Request, invalid_grant Pass
TC-003 GET /streetview/refresh/invalid-refresh-token?stage=prod Invalid refresh token Controlled JSON error 400 Bad Request, {"message":"Failed"} Pass with note
TC-004 POST /streetview/publish?stage=dev&platform=web Well-shaped invalid publish payload Controlled JSON error, no publish 400 Bad Request, {"message":"Failed fetch panorama","code":4} Pass
TC-005 POST /streetview/publish?stage=dev&platform=web {} 400 Bad Request validation JSON 502 Bad Gateway HTML Fail
TC-006 GET /streetview/invalid-google-code?stage=dev&platform=web Invalid dev auth code Controlled JSON error 502 Bad Gateway HTML Fail
TC-007 GET /streetview/refresh/invalid-refresh-token?stage=dev Invalid dev refresh token Controlled JSON error 502 Bad Gateway HTML Fail

Bug Summary Table

Bug Evidence Impact Developer Note
Malformed publish payload returns gateway error TC-005 returns 502 Bad Gateway for {} Client cannot distinguish validation error from service failure Validate req.body.pose.latLngPair before destructuring in routes/streetview.js:158-160
Dev-stage OAuth error returns gateway error TC-006 returns 502 Bad Gateway Save/connect Street View account failure is not handled consistently on dev stage Ensure dev-stage Google OAuth errors are caught and returned as JSON
Dev-stage refresh error returns gateway error TC-007 returns 502 Bad Gateway Token refresh/account reconnect failures are hard to debug Return structured 400/401 JSON instead of nginx HTML
Refresh error response is too generic TC-003 returns only {"message":"Failed"} Developer/support has minimal error context Include safe error reason/code without exposing secrets

Live API Evidence

TC-001 API availability baseline

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/

Payload: none

Response:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

Body excerpt:

API running well
v1.1.2

Result: Pass. Service was reachable during the test window.

TC-002 Invalid prod Google auth code

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/streetview/invalid-google-code?stage=prod&platform=web

Payload: path param googlecode=invalid-google-code, query stage=prod&platform=web

Response:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"Failed","error":{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Malformed auth code."}}

Result: Pass. Invalid auth code returns controlled JSON response.

TC-003 Invalid prod refresh token

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/streetview/refresh/invalid-refresh-token?stage=prod

Payload: path param refreshtoken=invalid-refresh-token, query stage=prod

Response:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"Failed"}

Result: Pass with improvement note. Error is controlled, but response is too generic for troubleshooting account-save failures.

TC-004 Well-shaped invalid publish payload

Endpoint: POST https://node.panorra.com/streetview/publish?stage=dev&platform=web

Payload:

{
  "post_slug": "invalid-slug",
  "access_token": "invalid-access-token",
  "pose": {
    "latLngPair": {
      "latitude": 43.6532,
      "longitude": -79.3832
    }
  }
}

Response:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"Failed fetch panorama","code":4}

Result: Pass. The endpoint returned a controlled error for invalid data without publishing.

TC-005 Malformed publish payload

Endpoint: POST https://node.panorra.com/streetview/publish?stage=dev&platform=web

Payload:

{}

Response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: text/html

<h1>502 Bad Gateway</h1>

Result: Failed. Missing pose.latLngPair should return validation error JSON, not a gateway failure.

TC-006 Invalid dev Google auth code

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/streetview/invalid-google-code?stage=dev&platform=web

Payload: path param googlecode=invalid-google-code, query stage=dev&platform=web

Response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: text/html

<h1>502 Bad Gateway</h1>

Result: Failed. Dev-stage OAuth error should be caught and returned as controlled JSON like the prod-stage invalid code test.

TC-007 Invalid dev refresh token

Endpoint: GET https://node.panorra.com/streetview/refresh/invalid-refresh-token?stage=dev

Payload: path param refreshtoken=invalid-refresh-token, query stage=dev

Response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: text/html

<h1>502 Bad Gateway</h1>

Result: Failed. Dev-stage refresh error should be caught and returned as controlled JSON.

Confusion Matrix

Classification Count Cases
True Positive 3 TC-001, TC-002, TC-004
True Negative 1 TC-003
False Positive 0 None
False Negative 3 TC-005, TC-006, TC-007

Final Verdict

Bug confirmed. Street View error handling is not consistently safe: malformed publish payloads and dev-stage OAuth/refresh failures return 502 Bad Gateway. The publish route needs request validation before destructuring, safer upstream JSON parsing, and controlled error responses for all Street View account-save failure paths.

QA Summary - Issue #3: Update Node for Share to Facebook

Status: Passed
Date: 2026-07-22
Scope: Live API hit + source review against https://node.panorra.com

Result

Issue #3 asks the download/share helper to "Only return url". I tested the exact URL from the task with real image data. QA Summary - Issue #6: Handle Issue Failed Node

Scope: Live API hit + source review against https://node.panorra.com

Result

Issue #6 asks to handle the failed add-account flow. I tested the Google/Street View add-account error path with invalid real requests. The current /streetview/:googlecode endpoint returns controlled 400 Bad Request JSON for invalid Google auth codes on both prod and dev stages. No HTTP 500 was returned for the add-account endpoints tested.

I did not run a valid Google OAuth account connection because that requires a real authorization code and can mutate account state.

  • routes/streetview.js:43-51 logs OAuth request diagnostics while masking whether the client secret exists instead of printing the secret value.
  • routes/google_api.js:203-223 is a separate legacy-style Google auth endpoint that returns only { "message": "Failed" }; it is less informative than /streetview/:googlecode, but the issue evidence matches the structured /streetview failure shape.

issues.main_description_html:
• The service resillent to rebooting the machine

QA Summary - Issue #7: Handle Issue Redis Toronto Is Not Working on Recomendation for You

Status: Failed / Bug confirmed
Date: 2026-07-22
Scope: Live API hit + source/deploy review against https://node.panorra.com

Result

Issue #7 asks that the service be resilient to machine reboot. I did not reboot the production machine because that is an infrastructure-impacting action and requires explicit confirmation. Safe validation found that the service is currently reachable, but the repository does not contain a reboot-resilience setup such as pm2 startup, pm2 save, systemd unit files, Docker restart policy, or Redis reconnect/health logic.

The codebase also does not expose a Recommendation-for-You or Toronto Redis endpoint in this node-panorra service. Redis is present as a dependency in package.json, but source search found no Redis client usage in the app routes.

No HTTP 500 was returned in the safe live API checks.

Code Review Summary

  • package.json includes redis, but repo search found no Redis client connection or Redis error/reconnect handling in app.js or routes/*.
  • app.js:60-67 only mounts /, /notification, /download, /share, /streetview, /google-api, and /stream; no recommendation endpoint exists in this service.
  • ansible-deploy.yml:22-34 starts or restarts node-panorra with PM2, but does not run pm2 startup or pm2 save.
  • bin/www starts a normal HTTP server, but does not add process-level crash/restart or dependency health behavior.

  • Black-box: Real HTTP calls to production host.
  • Gray-box: Live availability result compared against issue scope and mounted route behavior.
